## Contract Template

A standard starting point per contract type: `templateName`, `contractType`, `useCase`,
`bodyMarkdown`, `guidance`, `requiredInputs`, `isPublished`, and `standardClauses` linked to
the **Clause** library.

```ts
import { ContractTemplate } from '../contract-template';
@field template = linksTo(ContractTemplate);
```

**Clauses are linked, never copied.** A template that retyped its own clause text would let
the library and the templates disagree — the drift the clause library exists to prevent.

**`isPublished` is a gate, not decoration.** Juro's publish/unpublish exists so a standard
cannot change under a review already running; the same reasoning applies to a template, and
the fitted view marks a draft so nobody picks one by accident.

**`requiredInputs` is the useful half.** It is what a drafter must supply before the template
is usable, and writing it down is what stops it living only in one person's head.

### Non-goals

Does not generate a document — the spec puts document generation explicitly out of scope, so
this is a starting *position*, not a factory. Does not own clause text (**Clause** does) or
deviation tracking (**ContractClause** does). Does not enforce that a contract created from
it actually uses the linked clauses.
